content.value_statement: Feature ideas often lack clear requirements, tradeoffs, and implementation steps. This skill guides discovery, design validation, documentation, and task planning through structured dialogue.
actual_capabilities: Explores project structure and existing patterns before planning a feature.
Collects core, technical, integration, and documentation requirements through batched questions.
Compares two or three implementation approaches with pros and cons.
Builds sectioned design documents covering architecture, data, API, components, errors, and tests.
Produces implementation task checklists with priorities, dependencies, files, and estimates.
limitations: It is a planning workflow, not an implementation engine.
It depends on accurate user answers and repository context.
It does not validate generated designs by running tests.
It may need adaptation when AskUserQuestion tooling is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: A product engineer can turn a broad idea into requirements, architecture, and task breakdowns before coding.

use_cases.title: Compare Implementation Approaches
use_cases.description: A technical lead can evaluate options, risks, dependencies, and quality requirements with clear tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: A developer can create design documentation and ordered tasks for a later coding session.

prompt_templates.title: Start Feature Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small or unclear feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a small feature. Start by asking the core requirement questions and then summarize the answers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Across System Layers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a feature that affects multiple parts of an application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository context and help design [feature]. Ask technical, dependency, and documentation questions before proposing approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Architecture Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for comparing design tradeoffs before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [feature] for a system with [constraints]. Compare three approaches, recommend one, and validate each design section before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Create Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for turning an approved design into implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce a full implementation handoff for [feature]. Include requirements, architecture, API, error handling, tests, and prioritized tasks.

output_examples.input: I need a saved search feature for our app.
output: The skill asks about users, scope, system layers, integrations, and testing needs.
It then recommends an approach and drafts a design outline.

output_examples.input: We need to redesign our API error handling.
output_examples.output: The skill gathers reliability and compatibility requirements, compares failure strategies, then creates tasks for tests and implementation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for a planned admin dashboard.
output: The skill creates a design document outline with requirements, architecture, components, errors, and tests.
It also generates prioritized implementation tasks with dependencies and estimates.

best_practices: Share repository context and existing feature patterns before answering design questions.
Choose recommendations only after reviewing tradeoffs, dependencies, and quality requirements.
Validate each design section before moving to implementation tasks.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow for tiny changes that only need a direct edit.
Skipping requirement questions and asking for a final design immediately.
Treating generated tasks as verified estimates without developer review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides feature planning through requirement questions, approach comparison, design validation, and implementation handoff.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on design documents and task plans before code implementation.

faq.question: Can it handle large features?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for features that touch multiple layers, teams, or quality requirements.

faq.question: Does it require a specific programming language?
faq.answer: No. It adapts to the repository structure, architecture, and conventions it can inspect.

faq.question: What files can it create?
faq.answer: It can propose design documents and task lists. File creation depends on the active agent environment.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It plans changes and asks for validation before implementation. Review designs before changing sensitive systems.
